facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Phosphatotitan was discovered in the Sidi Chennane phosphate mine within the Ouled Abdoun Basin in Khouribga Province, Morocco.
facts.quote: The Phosphatotitan fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Sidi Chennane phosphate mine (Lower Couche III) of the Ouled Abdoun Basin in Khouribga Province, Morocco.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a fragmentary skeleton including dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae and parts of the pelvis.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a fragmentary associated skeleton comprising some vertebrae (one dorsal (trunk vertebra, a sacrum with at least four vertebrae, and one caudal (tail) vertebra) and parts of the pelvis (fragmentary ilium, both pubes, and possibly part of the ischium).

facts.statement: The linear dimensions of Phosphatotitan fossils are approximately 39.75% of those of Patagotitan.
facts.quote: With a dorsal vertebral centrum height of 15.9 cm, the linear dimensions of the Phosphatotitan fossils are about 39.75% of those of Patagotitan.

facts.statement: The estimated weight of Phosphatotitan is between 3.5 and 4.3 tonnes.
facts.quote: As such, its weight can be calculated to be between 3.5 and 4.3 t, around 6.3% of the mass of Patagotitan.

facts.statement: Phosphatotitan lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
Phosphatotitan lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Phosphatotitan has been recorded.
Phosphatotitan is classified as a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
Phosphatotitan belongs to the clade Lognkosauria, which otherwise contains only South American members.
facts.quote: These taxa are part of the larger clade Lognkosauria, whose only other definitive members are also South American.

facts.statement: Phosphatotitan is classified within the family Argentinosauridae.
Researchers suggest that Phosphatotitan's small size may be due to island dwarfism or environmental conditions favoring smaller herbivores in the latest Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Longrich et al. (2026) suggested that the small size of Phosphatotitan in relation to other lognkosaurs may be due to either island dwarfism (in the event that Morocco was possibly separated from parts of the African continent), or conditions of environments during the latest Cretaceous, wherein smaller herbivore diversification was favored over that of giant taxa.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the relationship between Moroccan and South American titanosaurs reflects ancient wide distribution or complex oceanic dispersal patterns.

rejected.quote: In 2026, Nicholas R. Longrich and colleagues described Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis as a new genus and species of titanosaur based on these fossil remains.

rejected.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses using an updated version of the dataset of Pérez-Moreno et al. (2024), Longrich et al. (2026) recovered Phosphatotitan as the sister taxon to an unnamed Moroccan specimen from the Sidi Daoui locality.
